requirements.evidence: Routes/names and throttle are present (routes/web.php:14-20), the phpunit locale pins are added (phpunit.xml:22-24), and the theme CSS uses #0f7490 (resources/views/vendor/mail/html/themes/pegafila.css:2); but the reset flow leaks account existence (app/Http/Controllers/Auth/PasswordResetController.php:28-30), the required subject translations are absent (lang/pt_BR.json is not in the diff), mail.markdown.paths is emptied (config/mail.php:104), and the theme Blade file would shadow the CSS once that path is restored (resources/views/vendor/mail/html/themes/pegafila.blade.php:1-16).

conventions.evidence: Four fields/six rules are validated inline instead of with a Form Request (app/Http/Controllers/Auth/PasswordResetController.php:40-51); controllers rely on the default base controller's $this->middleware() (PasswordResetController.php:15, VerifyEmailController.php:12); migrations are hand-written named classes (database/migrations/2026_10_29_000000_create_users_table.php:7); imports are not Pint-ordered (PasswordResetController.php:7-9, database/factories/UserFactory.php:7-8); no CHANGELOG/docs update.

security.evidence: CSRF and escaping are correct (resources/views/auth/forgot-password.blade.php:11-14), and EmailVerificationRequest enforces the id/hash 403; however the unknown-address status reveals whether an account exists (PasswordResetController.php:28-30) and the model's 'password' => 'hashed' cast was removed (app/Models/User.php:25-27).

tests.evidence: Six tests exist (tests/Feature/PasswordResetTest.php:13-68) but cover only happy paths: no unknown-e-mail/enumeration test, no invalid-token/password-rule/remember-token/PasswordReset-event test, and no test of the verification route's auth/signed/403 behavior; the subject assertion at :63 compares __() to itself with the wrong key casing.

simplicity.evidence: The extra resources/views/vendor/mail/html/themes/pegafila.blade.php:1-16 duplicates the CSS theme and would shadow it, show() takes an unused $request (PasswordResetController.php:33), UserFactory adds a redundant $model (database/factories/UserFactory.php:12), and the model/factory rewrite is unnecessary.

readability.evidence: Controllers and views are short and understandable, but the User/UserFactory rewrite reverts the project's attribute/typed style (app/Models/User.php:14-27, database/factories/UserFactory.php:12-24) and the stray theme Blade file is a misleading duplicate of the CSS theme.

scope.evidence: app/Models/User.php:10-28 and database/factories/UserFactory.php:12-24 are rewritten far beyond adding MustVerifyEmail, deleting UserFactory::unverified() and the hashed cast; the routes, views, config, migrations and tests otherwise serve the task.

issues.explanation: $this->middleware() only exists on Illuminate\Routing\Controller; the default Laravel 11+ App\Http\Controllers\Controller is a plain abstract class, so unless this project's base controller still extends the routing one (not shown), both controllers will fatal at construction; register guest/auth/signed/throttle on the routes or implement HasMiddleware.

Password::sendResetLink() returns passwords.user for an unknown address and the controller flashes that status, so the response reveals whether the account exists; the task requires always flashing passwords.sent.

No pt-BR entries are added for the contract's subject keys 'Reset your password' and 'Verify your email address', so the notification subjects fall back to English instead of 'Redefina sua senha'/'Verifique seu endereço de e-mail'.
Setting mail.markdown.paths to [] drops resource_path('views/vendor/mail'), where html/themes/pegafila.css lives, so the custom theme cannot be located or inlined and markdown rendering may fail.

This extra file is not the contract's CSS theme; once mail.markdown.paths is corrected, Laravel resolves the theme as a view and searches .blade.php before .css, so this file would shadow pegafila.css and feed an HTML document (with @yield('content') and a non-existent mail::styles include) to the CSS inliner. The CSS file is the theme; the Blade file should be removed.

The migration creates password_resets, while Laravel 9+ password brokers default to password_reset_tokens with email as primary key; unless config/auth.php overrides the table (not shown), reset tokens cannot be stored or found.
Beyond implementing MustVerifyEmail, the change rewrites the model/factory style and deletes UserFactory::unverified(), which other tests may use; this unrelated churn can break sibling tests.

The 'password' => 'hashed' cast is removed, so the model no longer guarantees hashing on assignment; a future User::create/update with a plain password (such as the registration task) would store it in plaintext unless it hashes manually.
Four fields and six password rules are validated inline; the conventions call for a Form Request once rules grow beyond one or two fields.

Migrations are hand-written with named classes (class CreateUsersTable extends Migration) instead of the anonymous-class files produced by php artisan make:migration, contrary to the migration convention.
Imports are not alphabetically ordered (Password before Hash, Str before Hash), so ./vendor/bin/pint --test would fail.

Tests cover only happy paths; there is no test that an unknown e-mail still flashes passwords.sent, no invalid-token/password-rule/remember-token/PasswordReset-event test, and no test of the verification route's auth/signed/403 behavior.

The subject assertion compares __('Verify Your Email Address') with the notification subject using a differently-cased key than the contract's 'Verify your email address', so it either fails or passes without proving the Portuguese translation exists.
The contract places password-reset controllers directly under app/Http/Controllers and only verification under Auth; this controller is in Auth (functional, but a contract detail).
No CHANGELOG entry or docs update for the new password-reset/verification endpoints and mail theme, contrary to the 'Keep docs in sync' convention.

review.summary: The change wires up password-reset and verification routes, controllers, forms, phpunit locale pins and a PegaFila mail theme, but it is not mergeable: the controllers rely on $this->middleware() from a default base controller that no longer provides it, the reset flow reveals whether an e-mail exists, the pt-BR subject translations are missing, and the empty mail.markdown.paths prevents the custom theme from being found. Tests cover only happy paths and one subject assertion is self-referential.
